notes.text: That saw — Near fourscore years ago. This house - The temple built by Solomon.
My spirit — Of strength and courage, of wisdom and understanding.

Yet once — After many confirmations of the new covenant, one more, remains to be made. A little while - Tho' above five hundred years, yet this was but a little time compared with that between the promise to Adam and Christ's coming. I will shake - Whether it be metaphorical or literal, it was verified at the time of Christ's coming into the world. After the return of the captivity, by the commotions among the Grecians, Persians, and Romans, which began soon after this time; this was metaphorically fulfilled. And it was literally fulfilled by prodigies and earthquakes, at the birth, death, and resurrection of Christ.

All nations — Which was literally fulfilled in the overthrow of the Persian monarchy by the Grecians, in the civil wars, and succeeding troubles among Alexander's successors, the growth of the Roman power by subduing their neighbours, and their dissentions and home-bred wars. The desire - Christ the most desirable, to all nations, and who was desired by all that knew their own misery, and his sufficiency to save them who was to be the light of the Gentiles, as well as the glory of his people Israel. With glory - The first temple had a glory in its magnificent structure, rich ornaments, and costly sacrifices; but this was a worldly glory; that which is here promised, is a heavenly glory from the presence of Christ in it. He that was the brightness of his father's glory, who is the glory of the church, appeared in this second temple.
The silver — The treasures of both: doubt not therefore but I will give enough to build this house.
In this place — In my house, a type of Christ. Peace - A spiritual, internal, and heavenly peace.

glossa.text:
*Praise, for David himself.* ((CAS.)) This psalm contains briefly the things which in the divine Scriptures are spread abroad at large, etc., *as far as* lest any should be able to err in his praise:

((AUG.)) God fills the saints with the Holy Spirit, etc., *as far as* and therefore let his spirit in his servants praise him, because he makes himself to be praised.

((CAS.)) As there are seven psalms of penance, so also seven spirits, according to that sacrament wherein the Lord commanded Moses to set seven lamps in the tabernacle, shining with perpetual light.

*I will extol thee.* ((CAS.)) First the prophet promises endless praise; secondly, he says that all shall accomplish the praise of God in nine ways, there, *Generation and generation;* thirdly, he explains the same at greater length, there, *compassionate.*

*For ever and ever.* ((CAS.)) He who does not begin here shall be dumb in the world to come.

*Every day,* etc. ((ID.)) He who here every day does so, shall deserve in the eternal day to praise with continual exultation.

 ((AUG.)) He blesses now *every day,* that, when the one day without ends *fines*; read *fine*, "without end" shall have come, he may go from praise to praise, as from virtue to virtue. *For ever, and for ever and ever.* ((CAS.)) Of which praise elsewhere: *They shall praise for ever and ever ((Psal. XXXVIII))*, because they will always love him whom they will always see, since nothing is more delightful than that vision.
*Exceedingly.* ((CAS.)) In one word he has given us to consider that which cannot be fully grasped: and therefore never cease from praises.

*Generation and generation.* ((CAS.)) Secondly, he promises that all shall accomplish the praise of God in nine ways. *Thy works.* ((AUG.)) If we fail in his greatness, let us at least praise the worker from his works, the founder from the things founded, the creator from his creatures. ((CAS.)) Nine are the works: power, magnificence, holiness, wonders, strength, the greatness of terrible things, memory, justice, which shall be explained hereafter: from these, as from topics and seeds, all praise is drawn, in the manner in which all arguments are taken from a small number of topics. *And thy power.* ((AUG.)) For works do not praise, save that they may announce the strength of the worker. But certain eloquent men praise the creature, forgetful of the Creator. But holy praisers, if they love the works, praise the worker the more: and on account of these they love him. If in things made there is felt any beauty, usefulness, strength, it is the more praised in him who made it. If thou praisest the works, thou praisest thyself also, who art the work of God. And this occurs: *Let not thy own mouth praise thee, lest thou seem arrogant ((Prov. XXVII))*. But it is not arrogance, because thou praisest God in thee, not thyself.

notes.text: Our gathering together to him — In the clouds.

Be not shaken in mind — In judgment. Or terrified - As those easily are who are immoderately fond of knowing future things. Neither by any pretended Revelation from the Spirit, nor by pretense of any word spoken by me.

Unless the falling away — From the pure faith of the gospel, come first. This began even in the apostolic age. But the man of sin, the son of perdition - Eminently so called, is not come yet. However, in many respects, the Pope has an indisputable claim to those titles. He is, in an emphatical sense, the man of sin, as he increases all manner of sin above measure. And he is, too, properly styled, the son of perdition, as he has caused the death of numberless multitudes, both of his opposers and followers, destroyed innumerable souls, and will himself perish everlastingly. He it is that opposeth himself to the emperor, once his rightful sovereign; and that exalteth himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped - Commanding angels, and putting kings under his feet, both of whom are called gods in scripture; claiming the highest power, the highest honour; suffering himself, not once only, to be styled God or vice-God. Indeed no less is implied in his ordinary title, "Most Holy Lord," or, "Most Holy Father." So that he sitteth - Enthroned. In the temple of God - Mentioned Rev. xi, 1. Declaring himself that he is God - Claiming the prerogatives which belong to God alone.

glossa.text: *And we beseech you, brethren, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ,* etc. Thus far he has said that he gives thanks for them and prays; here he determines concerning the day of judgment, beseeching them that they do not lightly and readily take up an opinion concerning the coming of the Lord as of one close at hand, nor be terrified.

*Be not soon moved.* As if he should say: If you be moved; it is soon, for nothing is brought upon you which lasts long. *Nor by spirit.* That is, if a malignant spirit, appearing in a vision as an angel of light, should persuade you of this. Or, if any man should say that through the Holy Spirit revealing it he has come to know this, that the day of judgment is at hand, do not believe him. *Nor by epistle.* For prevaricators are wont, that they may deceive, to feign a letter under the name of some famous man, that the authority of the name may commend what by itself could not be received. *As if the day of the Lord were at hand.* He does not say this in such a way as not to wish that they should have their loins girt and lamps burning in their hands, waiting for when the Lord shall return from the wedding.

*In the temple.* Or, *the temple.* Some will have it that in this place not the prince himself only, but his whole body, that is, the multitude of men belonging to him together with the prince himself, is to be understood; and they think it more rightly said, as it is in the Greek, not *in the temple,* but *that he sit into the temple of God,* as though he himself with his own were the temple of God, which is the Church. As it is said: He sits into a friend, that is, as a friend.

*For unless there come.* He speaks covertly of the destruction of the Roman empire, lest he should provoke them to the persecution of the Church. Or he says this of the spiritual empire of the Roman Church, or of a departure from the faith. *Unless the deserter come first.* So some codices have it. And it is doubtful to none that he said this of Antichrist, whom he calls a deserter: from the Lord God, assuredly. For if this can deservedly be said of all the ungodly, how much more of this one! *The son of perdition.* Antichrist, not by nature, but by imitation.

notes.text: Matt. xxii, 23; Mark xii, 18.
Deut. xxv, 5.
The children of this world — The inhabitants of earth, marry and are given in marriage - As being all subject to the law of mortality; so that the species is in need of being continually repaired.
But they who obtain that world — Which they enter into, before the resurrection of the dead.
They are the children of God — In a more eminent sense when they rise again.

That the dead are raised, even Moses, as well as the other prophets showed, when he calleth — That is, when he recites the words which God spoke of himself, I am the God of Abraham, &c. It cannot properly be said, that God is the God of any who are totally perished. Exod. iii, 6.

He is not a God of the dead, or, there is no God of the dead — That is, tho term God implies such a relation, as cannot possibly subsist between him and the dead; who in the Sadducees' sense are extinguished spirits; who could neither worship him, nor receive good from him. So that all live to him - All who have him for their God, live to and enjoy him. This sentence is not an argument for what went before; but the proposition which was to be proved. And the consequence is apparently just. For as all the faithful are the children of Abraham, and the Divine promise of being a God to him and his seed is entailed upon them, it implies their continued existence and happiness in a future state as much as Abraham's. And as the body is an essential part of man, it implies both his resurrection and theirs; and so overthrows the entire scheme of the Sadducean doctrine.

glossa.text: *And there came to him,* etc. There were two heresies among the Jews: that of the Pharisees, who set foremost the righteousness of traditions and observances, whence also they were called the separated from the people; and that of the Sadducees, who likewise claimed for themselves what they were not, that is, just men.

*Master.* They who do not believe the resurrection of bodies, and think that souls perish with bodies, invent the baseness of a tale, which convicts of raving those who assert the resurrection. But it may be that this once happened in their own nation. *That he may take,* etc. In the law of the letter one was compelled to marry in this life. But in the law of the spirit chastity is commended.

*But they,* etc. Although all, both good and bad, are to rise again and to remain without marriage, yet the Lord, that he may stir men up to the glory of the resurrection, discourses of the elect alone. But if in the resurrection they shall neither take wives, then those bodies shall rise which are able to marry and to take in marriage. Which is said of those who have generative members, but shall be enslaved by no pleasure or necessity of marrying. And note that although he speaks secret mysteries with liers-in-wait and tramplers, yet he does not give what is holy to dogs; but there were present many fit persons who ought not to be neglected because of the uncleanness of others. *Neither shall they marry,* etc. Since marriages are for the sake of children, children for the sake of succession, succession for the sake of death, where therefore there is no death, neither are there marriages.
*But that the dead shall rise again.* After he had satisfied the question proposed concerning the conditions of the resurrection, he treats of the resurrection itself against their unbelief.

notes.text: My words — The words which I am now about to speak. And that which Job wished for, God granted him. His words are written in God's book; so that wherever that book is read, there shall this glorious confession be declared, for a memorial of him.
Lead — Anciently they used to grave the letters in a stone with an iron tool, and then to fill up the cuts with lead, that the words might be more plainly seen.

For — This is the reason of his confidence in the goodness of his cause, and his willingness to have the matter depending between him and his friends, published and submitted to any trial, because he had a living and powerful Redeemer to plead his cause, and to give sentence for him. My Redeemer - In whom I have a particular interest. The word Goel, here used; properly agrees to Jesus Christ: for this word is primarily used of the next kinsman, whose office it was to redeem by a price paid, the sold or mortgaged estate of his deceased kinsman; to revenge his death, and to maintain his name and honour, by raising up seed to him. All which more fitly agrees to Christ, who is our nearest kinsman and brother, as having taken our nature upon him; who hath redeemed that everlasting inheritance which our first parents had utterly lost, by the price of his own blood; and hath revenged the death of mankind upon the great contriver of it, the devil, by destroying him and his kingdom; and hath taken a course to preserve our name, and honour, and persons, to eternity. And it is well observed, that after these expressions, we meet not with such impatient or despairing passages, as we had before; which shews that they had inspired him with new life and comfort. Latter day - At the day of the general resurrection and judgment, which, as those holy patriarchs well knew and firmly believed, was to be at the end of the world. The earth - The place upon which Christ shall appear and stand at the last day. Hebrew. upon the dust; in which his saints and members lie or sleep, whom he will raise out of it. And therefore he is fitly said to stand upon the dust, or the grave, or death; because then he will put that among other enemies under his feet.

Though — Though my skin is now in a great measure consumed, and the rest of it, together with this body, shall be devoured by the worms, which may seem to make my case desperate. Flesh - Or with bodily eyes; my flesh or body being raised from the grave, and re-united to my soul. God - The same whom he called his Redeemer, ver. 25, who having taken flesh, and appearing in his flesh or body with and for Job upon the earth, might well be seen with his bodily eyes. Nor is this understood of a simple seeing of him; but of that glorious and beatifying vision of God, which is promised to all God's people.

See — No wonder he repeats it again, because the meditation of it was most sweet to him. For - For my own benefit and comfort. Another - For me or in my stead. I shall not see God by another's eyes, but by my own, and by these self-same eyes, in this same body which now I have. Though - This I do confidently expect, tho' the grave and the worms will consume my whole body.

glossa.text:
« For I know that my Redeemer, etc. » He said not maker, but openly declaring him Redeemer, who, after he had created all things, redeemed us from captivity by his own passion. And he lives who lay dead among the hands of the impious.

« And in the last day I shall rise out of the earth, and again, etc. » ((Ibid.)) Because the resurrection, etc., *as far as* in which flower he is shown to be a priest, who intercedes for us.

« Whom I myself shall see, etc. » ((GREG.)) Our flesh after the resurrection shall be the same and diverse. The same by nature, diverse by glory. And it shall be spiritual, because incorruptible and palpable: because it shall not lose the essence of a true nature. « I myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not to others. » He expressly indicates the truth of the resurrection: for it is not that one dies and another rises again (as those say who hold that the body shall be invisible and impalpable, as Eutychius said) but the very same.


« This my hope is laid up in my bosom. » We believe that we have nothing more certain, etc., *as far as* whence he straightway adds:

[0811B]

notes.text: The right — Regard my righteous cause.
Sentence — Judgment on my behalf. Come - From thy tribunal.

Proved — Or, searched or tried it, by many temptations and afflictions. Night - When mens minds being freed from the distraction of business, and from the society of men, they act more vigourously and freely, according to their several inclinations. Tried - As gold-smiths do metals. Nothing - Nothing of unrighteousness. Purposed - I have resolved, upon deliberation, as the word implies. Mouth - I am so far from practicing against Saul's life, as they charge me, that I will not wrong him so much as in a word.

Concerning — Observing the works of the men of this age, how wicked they are, I was resolved to take more care in ordering my own actions. By - By the help of thy blessed word. Paths - The customs and practices. Destroyer - Or, of the violent man: such as Saul, and his courtiers and soldiers.
By — By thy great power.

glossa.text: *The prayer of David.* ((CASS.)) The prayer belongs to the person of the Lord, the Church being joined to him, which is his body. *Hear, O Lord. ((Ibid.))* This psalm makes us attend to the true nature of his humanity. The prayer of Christ is an instruction of the faithful: as by weeping over Lazarus he taught us to have charity toward our neighbour; he fled his persecutors, that he might take from us the boldness of ill-considered rashness. First, he asks that it be rendered to him according to justice. *Not in deceitful lips.* As one who is unjustly condemned; or, as one who says: Lord, Lord, and does not do the works. ((AUG.)) Or, let my judgment come forth from thy countenance not in deceitful lips, so that in judging I may not put forth anything other than I understand.

*From thy countenance.* ((CASS.)) That is, according to those things which thou knowest in me, who have no sin. *Judgment.* Whereby he who was judged may be seen to have come forth as his own. *From thy countenance,* not from the disposition of the Jews, which deed is plain in the resurrection. Or, *judgment,* whereby he discerns all things.
*Thou hast proved.* ((CASS.)) From the likeness of a furnace, etc., *as far as* thou knowest me to be pure.

*Hard ways. ((Ibid.))* Namely the works of men: which, namely, the works of men deserve. Or, which men ought to imitate, for whom the road of the vices is easy, that of the virtues hard. Or, it was not found, so that he should not speak, that is, that I may not say these things boastfully, or, that I may not sin with my tongue, which is the work of men. ((AUG.)) Or, the hard ways of the thief, etc., *as far as* after I had gone along the hard ways and completed my steps.

*Perfect thou.* ((CASS.)) Even to the end: before that there is nothing but a beginning. Steps, that is, human actions, so that they who wish to imitate may not be moved away from thee, nor their footsteps from them.

*I have cried. ((Ibid.))* Secondly, he prays that his purity be delivered from the ambushes of the Jews. I too have cried, as though thou shouldst say, this belongs to none but the just man, who prays with confidence, because he knows he is heard.
*Make wonderful.* ((AUG.)) Wonderful are the things that are new: these are the things which he yielded in the flesh, the Jews marvelling.

*The apple of the eye.* It is very small, and yet through it the keen edge of sight is directed, whereby light and darkness are distinguished, just as through the humanity of Christ the godhead is what discerns between the good and the evil.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Hear a just cause, O Lord; attend to my cry.
I know that my Redeemer lives.
From my flesh I shall see God.
I know that my Redeemer lives.
He is God not of the dead, but of the living.
Come, let us worship. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: From the ash heap, stripped of everything, Job says the thing that should not be sayable: I know.
I know that my Redeemer lives.
O that my words were carved in rock forever — my Redeemer lives, and stands at last upon the earth.
I know that my Redeemer lives.
For our God is the God of the living; to him all of them are alive.
I know that my Redeemer lives.
So we worship in hope that outlasts the grave, sheltered in the shadow of God's wings.
I know that my Redeemer lives!
